advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend _package_file_climb to also match dotted module __file__ owners (arg.value being an ast.Attribute chain), not just bare ast.Name, so the guard cannot be evaded by `Path(pkg.sub.__file__)`.
evidence: tests/unit/test_repo_root_install_agnostic.py:89: `return (isinstance(arg, ast.Attribute) and arg.attr == "__file__" and isinstance(arg.value, ast.Name))`

Guard docstring claims it prevents this class from silently regressing (lines 12-15), but the ast.Name restriction leaves dotted `pkg.sub.__file__` reaches undetected — a check whose miss is a silent pass (fail-open oracle).
The pre-change code it replaced used bare-name forms (e.g. `Path(passes.__file__)`), so today's coverage is adequate, but any dotted variant added later evades detection.
advisory.finding: The structural guard's _package_file_climb only recognizes a package __file__ climb when the __file__ owner is a bare ast.Name (line 92: `isinstance(arg.value, ast.Name)`). A dotted form such as `Path(rebar.config.__file__).parents[3] / "docs"` has arg.value = ast.Attribute and is NOT detected, so a future test reaching a repo-root-only artifact through a dotted package __file__ passes the guard silently — the same non-editable-install regression the guard exists to catch.
scenarios: A new test writes `Path(rebar.llm.plan_review.passes.__file__).parents[4] / "docs" / "x.md"` — it reaches out of the installed package but the guard reports no offenders.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _package_file_climb, accept arg.value that is either an ast.Name or an ast.Attribute chain terminating in an ast.Name (e.g. walk .value until a Name), so dotted `pkg.sub.__file__` climbs are also detected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive-control assertion that _scan() (or _Scanner) returns a violation on an inline known-bad snippet for both shapes — a repo-root-only segment joined onto a Path(pkg.__file__) climb, and a WheelBuilder/SdistBuilder call given such a climb — and that the _OK_MARKER suppresses it.
evidence: The scan runs only over tests/*.py which are all now converted, so offenders is expected empty; nothing asserts the scanner returns a non-empty result on a KNOWN violating snippet (e.g. `Path(rebar.__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scripts"` or `WheelBuilder(str(Path(rebar.__file__).parents[2]))`).
_OK_MARKER (tests/unit/test_repo_root_install_agnostic.py:55) is defined but never exercised by any test either.
advisory.finding: The new structural guard test_tests_do_not_reach_repo_root_via_package_file asserts only ABSENCE (`assert not offenders`) over the already-converted test tree, with no positive control that the AST scanner actually detects a violating input. If any matcher (_package_file_climb, _leftmost, visit_BinOp, visit_Call, _unwrap_str) were broken so it matched nothing, the test stays green vacuously — the 'cannot silently regress' guarantee the diff claims is unverified. This is a fail-open oracle: the absence result is indistinguishable from a detector that never fires.
scenarios: A future edit breaks a scanner branch (e.g. renames an ast node kind or mishandles the `str(...)` unwrap) so no violation is ever flagged; the guard still passes and a reintroduced package-__file__ climb silently ships, re-reddening the non-editable sweep.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that parses inline source strings such as `ROOT = Path(rebar.__file__).resolve().parents[2]\nx = ROOT / "scripts" / "s.py"` and `WheelBuilder(str(Path(rebar.__file__).parents[2]))`, invoking _Scanner/_scan, and asserts the violation lineno IS reported (and that appending `# install-agnostic-ok` suppresses it).
